neighbours.label: The end of a specialist term for a land or heritage feature (petroglyphs, scoria, scarps, erratics, redds, rock-cut); everyday nouns in the same frame stay low.
fire: Hikers admired the pictographs on the canyon wall.
The cone is made of loose volcanic cinders and tuff.
Geologists mapped the drumlins left by the ice.
Fish lay their eggs in gravel spawning redds.
The moraines and eskers mark where the glacier stopped.
A rock-hewn chapel stands above the gorge.
Tall hoodoos rise above the badlands.
quiet: Hikers admired the sunset from the canyon wall.
The cone is made of vanilla ice cream and wafer.
Geologists mapped the roads left by the army.
Fish lay their eggs in the shallow water.
The fences and gates mark where the farm stopped.
A small chapel stands above the town.
Tall trees rise above the meadows.

notes: Probes: 0.63-0.78 on such terms; near misses 0.005-0.15, but 'Boulders' read 0.35 and 'tomb' 0.24, so plain landscape words leak.
